prompt.text: STRIDE is a threat-modelling checklist; the S stands for

answer.text: STRIDE is a threat-modelling checklist; the S stands for spoofing.

cards.fullLine: STRIDE is a threat-modelling checklist; the S stands for spoofing.

teaching.text: STRIDE covers spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service and elevation of privilege. Walking the list makes missing threats easier to spot.

teaching.alt: A beginner walkthrough of STRIDE threat modelling

cards.summary: Trust must change at a boundary

prompt.text: A trust boundary is where data crosses between zones with different

answer.text: A trust boundary is where data crosses between zones with different trust levels.

hints: The browser and the server sit on different sides.
cards.fullLine: A trust boundary is where data crosses between zones with different trust levels.

teaching.text: Every input crossing a trust boundary must be validated on the side that trusts it. A browser check protects the user; a server check protects the system.

teaching.alt: A diagram of browser, service and database zones separated by trust boundaries

cards.summary: Least privilege gives only what is needed

prompt.text: Least privilege gives each component only the

answer.text: Least privilege gives each component only the permissions it needs.

hints: Not the maximum it could use.
cards.fullLine: Least privilege gives each component only the permissions it needs.

teaching.text: A reporting job should read, not delete. A service account should reach one bucket, not the whole account. Small permissions turn a breach into a smaller incident.
Authentication proves identity. Authorization decides what that identity may do. A user can log in correctly and still have no right to open an admin page.

teaching.alt: A brass padlock hanging on a dark metal fence

cards.summary: Secrets do not belong in code

prompt.text: Where should an API key live?

answer.text: A secret manager or CI secret store.

options: A secret manager or CI secret store
A screenshot in the issue tracker
correct: A secret manager or CI secret store

teaching.text: Once a secret is committed, assume it is leaked. Store secrets outside the repository, inject them at run time and rotate them on a schedule.

prompt.text: controls so one failure does not expose everything.

answer.text: Defense in depth uses several independent controls so one failure does not expose everything.

hints: The word means they do not depend on each other.
cards.fullLine: Defense in depth uses several independent controls so one failure does not expose everything.

teaching.text: Validate input, enforce permissions, encrypt data and monitor for abuse. If one control fails, the next still stands. All four should not rely on the same assumption.

prompt.text: The OWASP Top 10 is a list of common web application

answer.text: The OWASP Top 10 is a list of common web application risks.

hints: Broken access control sits at number one in 2021.
cards.fullLine: The OWASP Top 10 is a list of common web application risks.

teaching.text: The 2021 list starts with broken access control, then cryptographic failures and injection. It is a starting checklist, not a complete security programme.

cards.summary: SLSA grades the build supply chain

answer.text: Levels of supply-chain integrity for build artifacts.

options: Levels of supply-chain integrity for build artifacts
correct: Levels of supply-chain integrity for build artifacts

hints: It is about proving how an artifact was built.

teaching.text: SLSA levels rise with the evidence behind a build: documented build, hosted build service, and hardened provenance. Higher levels make tampering harder and detectable.

teaching.search: What Is SLSA Supply Chain Levels for Software Artifacts
teaching.alt: An explanation of SLSA and its levels for software supply-chain security

cards.summary: An SBOM lists what went in

answer.text: An SBOM lists the dependencies that went into a build.

cards.fullLine: An SBOM lists the dependencies that went into a build.

teaching.text: A software bill of materials names every component and version in an artifact. When a library gets a CVE, the SBOM answers within minutes which products are affected.

teaching.alt: A source package moving through build, test and signing steps to become a verified artifact

cards.summary: Encrypt data in transit and at rest

prompt.text: Encryption in transit protects data while it travels; encryption at rest protects data when it is

answer.text: Encryption in transit protects data while it travels; encryption at rest protects data when it is stored.

cards.fullLine: Encryption in transit protects data while it travels; encryption at rest protects data when it is stored.

teaching.text: TLS covers the wire; disk and database encryption cover the stored copy. Neither helps if the application hands the data to the wrong user, so access control still matters.
